hints: Remember where astatine sits in Group 17, think about what happens as you move down the group from iodine to astatine.
Consider how atomic size affects the pull on bonding electrons, so decide if astatine will be more or less electronegative than iodine.
Link larger electron clouds to stronger London forces and higher boiling point, then decide what that means for how easily astatine evaporates.
walkthrough:
**Locate astatine in Group 17**

Think of the halogen family going down: fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, then astatine at the bottom. Astatine is directly below iodine, so it is larger with more electron shells and more shielding.

Trend down Group 17: atomic radius increases, nuclear attraction for outer electrons decreases.

**Predict electronegativity**

Electronegativity is the power of an atom to attract bonding electrons. Down the group the bonding electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded, so the pull gets weaker.

$$\text{electronegativity: } I > At$$
So astatine is expected to be less electronegative than iodine.

**Predict volatility**

Volatility is how easily a solid or liquid turns to vapour. It depends on boiling point, which for halogens depends on London (induced dipole-dipole) forces.

Astatine as $At_2$ has many more electrons than $I_2$, so it has stronger London forces, a higher boiling point and is harder to vaporise.

$$\text{stronger London forces} \rightarrow \text{higher boiling point} \rightarrow \text{lower volatility}$$
So astatine is expected to have lower volatility than iodine. Less electronegative plus lower volatility matches one row.

options.A: Electronegativity part is correct, astatine is less electronegative than iodine. However volatility is wrong because stronger London forces in larger $At_2$ give a higher boiling point, so astatine is less volatile, not more volatile.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. Astatine is larger and more shielded than iodine so it attracts bonding electrons less strongly, not more strongly. It also has stronger London forces so it is less volatile, not more volatile.
options.C: Correct on both trends. Down Group 17 electronegativity decreases so astatine is less electronegative than iodine. London forces increase so boiling point increases and volatility decreases, so astatine has lower volatility than iodine.
options.D: Volatility part is correct, astatine has lower volatility than iodine. However electronegativity is wrong because increased size and shielding down the group makes astatine less able to attract bonding electrons, not more.
